title: arbitrary-WHERE filtered vector search — INLINE (Custom Scan node, bitmap→membership) vs POST (native post-filter), SIFT1M
verdict: GO — INLINE dominates POST on BOTH recall and QPS at the selective regime where post-filter starves

dataset.name: SIFT1M
dataset.note: real SIFT neighbors — recall meaningful (M91 tie-density lesson)

params.index: v5 plain-vector IVF-AQ (separate_storage=1) — the realistic plain-(e)-index case

ground_truth: exact seqscan-filtered top-10 (WHERE <scalar> ORDER BY e <-> q LIMIT 10), same 100 SIFT queries
methodology: matched-recall / recall-QPS frontier (M45): POST = native vector index scan + Filter (enable_indexscan on, vecfilter off); INLINE = the Custom Scan node (bitmap sub-plan → TID membership → v5 Stage-1 inline skip + M91 adaptive probing), probe-swept

verdict_detail.1pct: INLINE (probes=64) recall 0.953 @ 266 qps vs POST recall 0.673 @ 21 qps — +0.28 recall AND ~12x QPS
verdict_detail.5pct: INLINE (probes=64) recall 0.915 @ 126 qps vs POST recall 0.593 @ 92 qps — +0.32 recall AND ~1.4x QPS
verdict_detail.why: POST (native post-filter) starves at selective filters — the vector index scan scores candidates then the executor Filter drops the non-matching, so the top-k is starved (the M87/M90 problem). INLINE pre-filters via the bitmap membership in Stage-1 (only matching candidates enter the rerank pool) + M91 adaptive probing, so recall is high AND the scan is fast.

correctness.note: the m93_t2 pg_tests prove the INLINE result is byte-identical to exact seqscan on a non-label column; pending + lossy-block rechecked; GUC-off path byte-identical (0 regression)

boundary: the inline pre-filter engages on both the v5 plain-vector and v7 label IVF-AQ layouts; the Custom Scan node is OFF by default (theodb.enable_vecfilter)
single run per point (the margin is large: +0.28 recall, up to 12x QPS)
the node's cost model is a spike heuristic (cost below cheapest to force selection); an honest cost model is a follow-up
NOT a QPS-superiority claim vs ScaNN/AlloyDB (paradigm ceiling M73/M82) — a capability + recall-QPS-Pareto result vs the native post-filter, measured
boundary: scalar WHERE over existing indexes; NOT the AlloyDB core cross-index mid-query re-plan (tier IV)
